issues.legal_issue: A civil suit by a transferee to determine whether property or an interest in it is evacuee property is barred when the property belonged to the evacuee and the governing statutory scheme provides remedies before the authorities.
material_facts: The claimant said that he had purchased land from its owner before that owner was declared an evacuee.
The claimant received notice to show cause why the land should not be declared evacuee property but did not appear before the authority.
The authority declared the land evacuee property, and the claimant did not pursue the available appeal or revision before filing a civil suit seeking a declaration of ownership.
The suit required the court to determine the claimant’s asserted right in property declared evacuee property.
issues.conclusion: The suit was barred by section 46(a) of the Administration of Evacuee Property Act; the claimant had to pursue the remedies provided under that Act.
issues.legal_principle: Section 46(a) bars civil and revenue courts from entertaining or adjudicating whether property, or a right or interest in it, is evacuee property. Where property belonged to an evacuee, a person claiming as a transferee must present the claim through the statutory process, including the appeal under section 24 and, if necessary, revision under section 27. No earlier cases were relied on; the Court said it was unnecessary to consider the cases cited.

predicates.civil_suit_seeks_adjudication_of_evacuee: A claimant brought a civil suit that required the court to decide whether property or an interest in it was evacuee property.
predicates.claimant_is_transferee_from_evacuating_o: The claimant asserted that the claimant received the property or an interest in it from its owner before that owner became an evacuee.
predicates.property_belonged_to_evacuating_owner: The property belonged to the person who was declared an evacuee.
predicates.statutory_remedies_are_available: The governing process allowed a person claiming an interest in the property to put forward the claim before the authorities and seek review through appeal or revision.

issues.definition: When a transferee brings a civil suit to determine the evacuee status of property that belonged to the evacuee, and the statutory process provides remedies for the claim, civil court jurisdiction is barred.

issues.legal_issue: An unregistered transfer does not pass title to immovable property when the applicable law requires a registered sale deed for a transfer of that kind.
material_facts: The claimant said he had purchased land and paid the agreed price, and he took possession.
The land was worth more than the applicable statutory threshold for requiring a registered sale deed.
No registered sale deed was executed in the claimant’s favour before the owner became an evacuee.
issues.conclusion: The claimant had not become the owner because no registered sale deed had been executed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the requirement that a registered sale deed is necessary to pass title to immovable property of the value established in this case. The judgment did not identify a specific statutory section for that requirement or rely on an earlier case for it.

predicates.ownership_claim_suit: A claimant brought a suit seeking recognition as the owner of immovable property.
predicates.transfer_value_exceeds_registration_thre: The value of the property was above the level at which the applicable law requires a registered instrument to transfer title.
predicates.no_registered_sale_deed_was_executed: The transferor and claimant did not execute a registered sale deed for the transfer.

issues.definition: If a claimant seeks ownership of property whose value requires a registered transfer instrument, but no registered sale deed was executed, title did not pass to the claimant.

issues.legal_issue: The protection for part performance cannot be used in a suit to establish ownership of property.
material_facts: The claimant relied on an alleged purchase, payment, and possession under an unregistered transfer.
The claimant’s suit sought a declaration that he was the owner and an order requiring a sale deed to be executed and registered.
The transferor was not seeking to recover the property in a proceeding against the claimant.
issues.conclusion: Section 53A of the Transfer of Property Act could potentially assist the claimant as a defence if the transferor sought to recover the property, but it could not establish the claimant’s ownership in this suit.
issues.legal_principle: Section 53A of the Transfer of Property Act affords protection by way of defence in the circumstances to which it applies; it does not enable a claimant to establish ownership through a suit seeking a declaration of title. No earlier cases were relied on for this proposition.

predicates.ownership_declaration_suit: A claimant brought a suit seeking a declaration that the claimant owns the property.
predicates.claimant_relies_on_part_performance_prot: The claimant relied on an alleged transfer and acts of performance to invoke protection based on part performance.
predicates.claimant_seeks_to_establish_title: The claimant sought to use that protection to establish ownership rather than only to resist a recovery claim by the transferor.

issues.definition: When a claimant relies on part-performance protection in a suit to establish ownership, that protection cannot establish the claimant’s title.
